transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-04-16 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Head of Research, Empower), Priya Sharma (Platform Eng), Grace Liu (VP Eng)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: Intro discovery focused on cost/unit economics for LLM use at Empower Capital. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment. Key asks: per-token unit costs, impact of batching and KV/prefix caching, budget constraints around $15k-$30k/month for initial pilot, and security/compliance requirements. Redwood to run benchmarks and send pricing/whitepaper.
Topics: per-token pricing, batching, KV cache, quantization, SLA/latency targets, VPC/private deployment, SOC2/KMS.
Action items (captured in metadata): see action_items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, work first, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Liam (Empower): Yep, loud and clear. Thanks, Maya.
[00:07] Maya: Cool. Quick intros? We'll keep it focused - Ethan our SE will dig into perf and cost stuff.
[00:12] Ethan (Redwood SE): Hi all.
[00:13] Grace (Empower): Grace here.
[00:15] Priya (Empower): Priya.
[00:16] Liam: Liam.

[01:05] Maya: The goal for today is to understand your workloads and cost constraints, so we can propose hosted vs dedicated vs private options. I think you mentioned budgets in the pre-read?
[01:15] Liam: Yeah, so for a pilot we're looking at maybe 100 to 200k tokens/day initially, with bursts. Budget wise, roughly 15k to 30k a month for the pilot. But most importantly low 100s of ms latency on core flows.
[01:32] Ethan: Ok, that's helpful. Can you talk about request patterns and prompt sizes? Average prompt + response token length?
[01:40] Priya: Average prompt per request is like 60 tokens, response around 120 tokens, but we have a tail with some longer analysis requests up to 1k tokens. Peak qps is around 30-40 reqs/s on trading hours, lower off-hours.
[02:00] Liam: Also we need retriev-augmented generation for some flows, so KV cache reuse could be high for certain prefixes.

[03:05] Ethan: Right. So from a unit economics lens, two levers matter: per-token pricing and effective token processing via batching and caching. With Redwood hosted pricing, you get per-token rates plus we automatically manage batching and prefix/KV cache optimizations; with Dedicated you get reserved capacity - lower per-token compute costs but you commit to capacity. Private is similar to Dedicated but customer-managed infra and a platform fee.
[03:34] Grace: Can you give ballpark numbers per token?

[03:40] Maya: Sure, to give a rough start - hosted for Llama-style open models we typically price in the X-X range depending on throughput SLOs, whereas Dedicated can reduce unit compute cost by 20-40% depending on utilization. Ethan, do you want to add numbers?
[03:56] Ethan: Yeah so for example on a 4k context model with mixed fp16 quantization, hosted list price might be about $0.0009 per input token and $0.0018 per output token —ignoring discounts—. If you go Dedicated with reserved GPUs at 70-80% utilization that could drop effective compute cost to something like $0.0005 in/ $0.0010 out per token. These examples vary a lot with sequence length and whether batching hits.
[04:30] Priya: Ok that's useful, but the arithmetic matters for us. If we do 200k tokens/day, that scales to what?
[04:36] Ethan: Quick math: 200k tokens/day times 30 days is 6M tokens/month. Multiply by say $0.0015 average per-token across in+out gives $9k/month. If you go dedicated and average drops to $0.0008 you get ~4.8k/month — but you then have reserved capacity costs.
[05:00] Liam: Reserved capacity meaning minimum monthly commitment for Dedicated?
[05:03] Maya: Right — Dedicated is typically a monthly commit for a GPU pool. Pricing depends on GPU type and size; we can show examples. There's also burst capacity for spikes.
[05:15] Grace: What about batching? We care about tail latency. If you batch aggressively you save cost but increase latency. We need p95 < 300ms for the primary flow.
[05:27] Ethan: Good point. Redwood runtime supports continuous batching that tries to respect latency SLOs. You can set per-route latency SLO targets; the runtime will trade batch size vs delay. For your p95 300ms we expect to see modest batching, often 2-4x efficiency gains on token scheduling depending on qps. For low qps flows, caching is bigger.
[05:51] Priya: Can you explain prefix/KV cache again? We have a lot of repeated contexts from similar prompts.
[05:58] Ethan: Sure. The KV cache (sometimes we say 'K-V' in transcripts) stores transformer key/value states for recent prefixes so if requests share a common prefix you avoid recomputing earlier attention, saving compute per token. For RAG flows where steps reuse an embedding or prompt prefix, effective per-token compute can drop by up to 60-80% on the reused portion. But it depends on reuse rate and windowing.
[06:25] Liam: Is that available on Hosted? Or only Dedicated/Private?
[06:29] Maya: Available across all modes; on Hosted we manage the cache multitenantly with safeguards, Dedicated gives you more control and isolation, and Private lets you manage the cache within your VPC.

[07:10] Priya: On security, we need SOC2, KMS, and SSO/SAML. We also need audit logs for model prompts for compliance.
[07:18] Maya: Redwood has SOC2, we integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated (we can support BYOK HSM in Private). We also surface audit logs and per-token tracing in the Console. I'll send the security whitepaper.
[07:32] Grace: How does encryption at rest work in Hosted? Data residency concerns?
[07:38] Ethan: Hosted encrypts at rest and in transit; keys are managed by Redwood unless you opt for Dedicated with customer-key options, or Private where keys never leave your KMS. For residency, we have region options in NA and EU; for strict residency Private is usually the path.

[08:15] Liam: Ok back to economics - what's the typical utilization we should expect to get to reach the Dedicated break-even?
[08:21] Ethan: Break-even depends on GPU type and your qps shape. As a thumb rule, for sustained throughput with steady qps you'd need around 60-70% utilization of the reserved pool to realize the 20-40% per-token saving vs Hosted after including Reservation amortization. If your workload is spiky, Hosted or a hybrid routing policy may be better.
[08:45] Priya: Do you support routing by policy so some traffic is hosted and some goes to Dedicated?
[08:50] Maya: Yes, smart routing is built-in. You can route by region, latency SLO, model variant, or cost. Common pattern: control-plane routes stable background traffic to Dedicated and burst or experimental traffic to Hosted.

[09:20] Grace: Can you walk through an example calculation including batching and cache?
[09:25] Ethan: Sure. Suppose baseline compute for a request without reuse is 1 unit. If batching gives 2x token throughput gain, effective cost per token halves. If KV cache saves 50% of tokens on average (reuse), that further halves compute. So if Hosted base is $0.0015, with good batching + caching you could see effective $0.000375 per token for those flows. But remember these are idealized — depends on reuse and latency SLO.
[10:00] Liam: That math makes sense. For our pilot many queries are reused during a session so caching should help.

[11:30] Priya: About quantization — do you offer different model precisions to trade quality vs cost?
[11:36] Ethan: Yes, Redwood recommends quantization profiles per-workload. E.g., int8/4-bit quantization can reduce compute and memory, enabling larger batch sizes or cheaper GPU types. We track quality regressions with evals. For critical flows we stick to fp16, but for less sensitive ones we can push heavier quantization and save cost.
[12:05] Grace: Any regressions observed when moving to int8?
[12:08] Ethan: Occasionally small quality differences; we run per-prompt eval suites and can flag regressions. Part of Redwood Optimize is giving recommendations and monitoring quality.

[13:00] Maya: Switching topics, what's your timeline and success criteria?
[13:06] Liam: We want a two-week pilot starting late April, show throughput and latency on our prompts, and get a clear monthly cost projection. Success is p95 under 300ms on main flow and unit cost < $0.001 per token effective across workload, or a clear path to that.
[13:22] Priya: Also we need to validate KMS integration and see audit logs flow.

[14:05] Ethan: Great. For the benchmark we'll need your sample prompt set and representative qps. Priya can upload that to the secure S3 link we'll send. We'll run hosted and a Dedicated-equivalent benchmark and share traces.
[14:20] Priya: We'll prepare the prompt set and a couple workload shapes — high reuse vs low reuse — and aim to deliver by Apr 18.

[15:00] Liam: About billing and attribution: if we start on Hosted and then move to Dedicated mid-pilot how does billing work for committed months?
[15:10] Maya: We can do a trial billing arrangement: Hosted pay-as-you-go for initial days, then a prorated Dedicated commit when you switch. We have flexible ramps for pilots. We'll send detailed options.

[16:00] Grace: Any hidden costs we should watch for? E.g., storage for caches or data egress?
[16:06] Ethan: Storage costs for KV caches are minimal compared to compute, but there can be egress if you move data across regions. Also model variants and larger context windows increase compute linearly. We itemize these in the pricing spreadsheet.

[17:40] Liam: For Dedicated, what GPU types do you recommend for our workload? We care about both latency and throughput.
[17:47] Ethan: For mixed latency and throughput, NVIDIA H100-like or A100-large are common; for cost-sensitive workloads we also support 80GB A40 or newer Ampere variants with quantization. We'll propose two configs: low-latency optimized (smaller batch, faster GPU) and cost-optimized (more batch, cheaper GPU).

[19:05] Priya: About region: we need EU data residency for a portion of traffic. Can Redwood Dedicated be deployed in our EU account?
[19:12] Maya: Yes, Dedicated and Private can be provisioned in EU regions; for Private we can run in your VPC. For Dedicated in EU we do an arrangement with regional capacity.

[21:00] Liam: Are there any cases where Hosted is strictly better and we should not try Dedicated?
[21:05] Ethan: Hosted wins for unpredictable spiky loads and very small pilots because you don't pay commit. If your utilization is low or highly spiky, Dedicated's commit overhead can make it more expensive. Also if you need on-prem isolated hardware due to compliance, Private is the route.

[22:30] Grace: Could you show an example of cost per thousand tokens for our pilot using your numbers?
[22:36] Maya: Sure: using the earlier example, hosted average across in+out might be $1.50 per thousand tokens; dedicated optimized might be $0.8 per thousand tokens assuming good utilization and caching. We'll put exact rows in the spreadsheet with assumptions.

[25:00] Liam: Any notes on reliability and fallbacks? We need graceful degradation in case of capacity issues.
[25:06] Ethan: Redwood has smart routing and automatic fallback: if Dedicated capacity is constrained we can fail over to Hosted model variants seamlessly. You can set fallback policies per-route.

[27:10] Priya: How long does setup take for Dedicated?
[27:14] Maya: Depends on capacity and region, typically 1-4 weeks for provisioning and testing. Private on-prem takes longer.

[29:00] Grace: Ok, let's capture agreements: Redwood runs benchmarks (hosted + dedicated equiv) using our prompt sets; Redwood sends pricing spreadsheet and security docs; follow-up call to review results.

[30:05] Ethan: Quick note on batching config — you can set max latency per-route, and the runtime uses continuous batching with per-route knobs. We'll include sample numbers like batch window 10-30ms, target p95 300ms, typical batch sizes 4-16 depending on qps.

[31:20] Liam: One more question: is there an SLA on latency or only uptime?
[31:26] Maya: We have uptime SLAs; latency SLOs are configurable and we can attach running metrics and alerts. For Dedicated we can guarantee latency targets in the contract with appropriate capacity guarantees.

[33:00] Priya: We'll also want to see token-level cost breakdown in Console.

[35:12] Grace: Ok that's helpful. Any other risks?
[35:15] Ethan: Main risk is overestimating caching reuse in production; we'll validate that in benchmark shapes. Also model quantization can introduce small regressions which we monitor.

[37:00] Liam: Thanks. When can we expect the benchmark and the materials?
[37:05] Maya: Pricing spreadsheet and security docs will go out today or tomorrow. Ethan will run the benchmark and aim to share results by 2026-04-21. Let's tentatively schedule a follow-up review on 2026-04-23.

[38:30] Priya: Sounds good. We'll upload prompts by Apr 18.

[40:00] Grace: One last thing — governance and role-based access: can we manage RBAC?
[40:05] Ethan: Yes, Console supports RBAC and integrates with SSO/SAML. We'll include role examples.

[42:00] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll send next steps in an email after the call.
[42:07] Liam: Thanks all.
[42:10] Priya: Thanks.
[42:12] Grace: Thanks.

[46:45] (call ends)
